answer: On an island, a falcon courier carries one membership credential per person. In-person registrars check for duplicate enrollment; an agent proves possession privately, and the ledger consumes one credential-derived nullifier per reward round. A zephyr of new wallet keys cannot reset that quota. Extra claims require recruiting more people and buying their cooperation rather than generating keys. This depends on honest registrars and effective duplicate checks. Bribery and credential rental remain possible, so it raises attack costs without proving every agent unique.
